text:
Predicates:
Supervised(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
Unsupervised(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
Reinforcement(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
UsedToTrain(x, y) ::: x is used to train y.
StateOfTheArt(y) ::: y is the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
Premises:
∀x (MachineLearningAlgorithm(x) → (Supervised(x) ∨ Unsupervised(x) ∨ Reinforcement(x))) ::: Machine Learning algorithms can be categorized as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
∀x (Unsupervised(x) → ¬RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data.
∃x (UsedToTrain(x, stateOfTheArtTextSummarization) ∧ StateOfTheArt(stateOfTheArtTextSummarization)) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
¬∃x (Reinforcement(x) ∧ UsedToTrain(x, stateOfTheArtTextSummarization)) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
∃x (UsedToTrain(x, stateOfTheArtTextSummarization) ∧ RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: The Machine Learning algorithm for training text summarization model requires labelled data.
Conclusion:
∃x (Supervised(x) ∧ UsedToTrain(x, stateOfTheArtTextSummarization)) ::: Supervised learning is used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
